en: The *Aṣṭama-prabhāsvara-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavān was dwelling in Śrāvastī at the Jetavana Grove.
At the Jetavana Grove,
together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
as well as immeasurable and innumerable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Surrounded on all sides by a great assembly of various kinds, including devas, humans, asuras, and others,
the World-Honored One then addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Noble son, as for the various supreme vidyās that you uphold,
the mantra deities employ fierce power such that their accomplishments are difficult to achieve;
though they may bring benefit later, they might cause temporary harm at first."
Now there is an eightfold named Universal Secret Mantra (Pumimi Shen-zhou).
Its majestic power is vast, its undertakings are easily accomplished,
and its divine efficacy is secret, remaining unimpaired from beginning to end.
"Those who are able to receive and uphold it will certainly obtain benefit and happiness.
I shall now speak it for you; do you wish to hear it?
At that time, Vajrapāṇi was filled with joy and leaped for gladness.
Prostrating at the Buddha’s feet, kneeling on the right knee with palms joined,
he requested, saying, "World-Honored One, I pray that you will explain this for us.
The Buddha said, "Listen attentively and reflect well upon it."
I shall now analyze and explain it for you.
What are the eight names of this Universal Secret Divine Mantra?
The first is named "Treasury of Merit."
The second was named Adorned Elephant Ear;
the third, Good Valor;
and the fourth, Cloud of Supreme Truth.
The fifth is named Blazing Accomplishment;
the sixth is named Subtle Form;
the seventh is named Adornment.
The eighth is named Vajra.
If anyone should hear these eight names of mantras,
they shall pass through seven koṭis of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of great kalpas in future ages.
They shall not fall into the realms of hell, animals, or hungry ghosts.
At the time of death, their body and mind will be peaceful and secure,
and they will see various Buddhas and Bodhisattvas appearing before them.
For them, he shall preach the essential points of the profound Dharma of the Mahāyāna.
Having heard this Dharma,
they will certainly attain rebirth in the Tuṣita Heaven to serve Maitreya.
Thereafter, he shall follow Maitreya down to Jambudvīpa;
his practices and vows will gradually increase until they reach their ultimate fulfillment.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

*Āṭe āṭe, vaṭe vaṭe, naṭe naṭe, kaṭe kaṭe, sume sume, sukhe, sarvakāmasādani, hiri miri vire vire, sidhyantu me sarvakāmasādhanīśvara-maṇḍala-pate svāhā.* When the Buddha had thus spoken this Samantaguhyadhāraṇī, [the assembly rejoiced].
Eight thousand koṭis of malevolent spirits and ghosts all gave rise to joy,
abandoned their poisonous minds, took refuge in the Buddha,
Dharma, and Saṅgha, and ceased evil while cultivating goodness.
They all went to where the Buddha was and uttered these words of solemn truth:
"We pray that you will always protect and uphold this great divine mantra,
so that those who receive and uphold it may have peace and happiness in body and mind."

The Buddha said, "Excellent! It shall be as you have wished. If there are sons or daughters of good family who take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, and Vajrapāṇi, and who are able to dwell in seclusion and steadfastly cultivate the holy life."
By drawing near to the caitya and upholding, reciting, and chanting [the teachings],
whatever virtuous aspirations one seeks shall all be attained,
even up to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
He constantly remembers his past lives without any forgetfulness.
When the Bhagavat had finished speaking this sutra,
Vajrapāṇi and all the other bodhisattvas—
Together with the devas, humans, asuras, and others—
all those in the assembly who heard what the Buddha had spoken were filled with great joy.
Believing, receiving, and practicing accordingly.
This is the eighth, the *Samantaguhyadhāraṇīsūtra*.
